question: Can a runtime capability/build gate, driver workaround, or kernel scheduling choice make the installed Honeykrisp fork (coopmat_f32_8=1) use the stable non-coopmat path without regressing decode or exact digests?
answer: No. The premise behind the question is inverted on current main: the fork's coopmat path is 1.95-3.09x FASTER than stock Mesa 26.1.7 on Q4 prefill, both paths produce identical (all six required) generated-token digests on the installed fork, and decode dispatches no coopmat kernel at all. Flipping the fork to the tile path is a measured 1.5-3.1x prefill regression with zero digest benefit on the installed driver, would additionally surrender the capability-gated native SDPA decode win (fork 96.0 vs stock 52.9 tok/s at 1053-token context), and would still not make bf16 outputs driver-portable: the tile path itself yields bf16_long c5be9207833d2a26 on stock but ad964232ee67fecd on the fork.

wheel.note: same wheel as receipts/2026-09-10-main-parity-12-matrix (commit f055acc2); 'harness=b6d662a-dirty' reflects untracked receipt/script files in the checkout, not library content; libmlx verified=match on every run

paired_matrix_fork_coop_vs_tile.protocol: Three alternating process pairs (coop: no MLX env; tile: MLX_OMARCHY_NO_COOPMAT=1) of the full bench_matrix run (2 pinned models x 3 README workloads, MLX_DISABLE_COMPILE=1, greedy temp 0 seed 0, 4 warmup tokens, --wheel provenance gate) on the installed fork, same wheel and venv throughout; 1-minute load < 1.5 before every run; AC power; /tmp/m1-gpu.lock serialization.

decode_tok_s_tile_per_coop_paired.note: per-pair medians are 0.97-1.02 on every leg; the three >1.1 values are pair-index-1 decode samples of one alternating cycle and have no structural mechanism (no coopmat kernel dispatches at matrix_m == 1); they are published unfiltered rather than dropped

kernel_microbench.method: direct worker (/tmp/qmm_worker.py, environment passed straight through): mx.quantized_matmul(f16 x [m,k], uint32-packed affine 4-bit/group-64 w, transpose=True) at the eight Qwen projection shapes, rng seed 17, 8 warmup + 16 timed evals, wall ms per eval; coop arm and MLX_OMARCHY_NO_COOPMAT=1 tile arm under /tmp/m1-gpu.lock

outputs_npz_sha256.interpretation: the two qmm paths are not bitwise equal at kernel level (different intra-dot accumulation order, both inside the qmm host-reference bound of receipts/2026-09-08-qmm-prefill-coopmat.json), yet the full-model generated-token digests are identical on every leg

kernel_microbench.invalid_first_attempt: a first profile attempt (profile-coop/, profile-tile/) was invalid and is excluded: its python wrapper stripped MLX_* before spawning the worker, so both arms ran the coopmat kernel (identical npz sha, no timing separation). The rerun passes the environment straight to the worker.

stock_digests.note: bf16_long is the only cross-driver digest divergence and it persists on the TILE path (coopmat=0 on stock), so the tile path is not driver-portable for bf16_long either; consistent with stock 26.1.7's unfixed sin/cos range-reduction and one-ulp division gaps in docs/known-defects.md

fork_vs_stock_premise_check.q4_prefill_consistency: parity-12 fork 1K prefill median 1112.5 vs this receipt's coop legs 1119.0/1075.6/1177.9
fork_vs_stock_premise_check.conclusion: the reported 'Q4 prefill much slower on the fork than stock' does not reproduce on main b6d662a8; the fork is the faster driver for Q4 prefill by 2-3x

findings: Premise inverted: on main b6d662a8 the installed fork's coopmat Q4 prefill (QmmPrefillCoopmatF16) is 1.95-3.09x faster than stock 26.1.7's tile path. There is no prefill regression on the fork to repair.
Both the coopmat and tile paths produce all six required generated-token digests on the installed fork; switching paths buys no digest change on the release driver.
The tile flip is a measured regression: 0.326-0.517 tile/coop prefill ratios on the Q4 model, 0.590-0.967 on bf16, and 3.4-3.6x slower qmm at large m in the kernel microbench.

Decode is structurally coopmat-free (qmm decode dispatches vec/subgroup kernels at matrix_m == 1; the native SDPA decode gate reads the capability bit, not the coopmat env); paired decode medians are 0.97-1.02 tile/coop. A capability-blind flip would also lose the fork's native SDPA decode (96.0 vs stock 52.9 tok/s at longctx).

The open cross-build portability defect (receipts/2026-09-10-prefill-qmm-isa/driver-portability-defect.json) is unaffected by this result: no scheduling choice measured here changes it, and its recorded candidate fix (on-device lowering probe at device creation with fallback to the composed path) remains the direction. Constraint added by this receipt for that work: the fallback (tile) path preserves the required Q4 digests on the installed driver, and the probe must keep the installed fork on the coopmat path.

policy.gpu_serialization: every M1 GPU command under flock -w 2400 /tmp/m1-gpu.lock with hard timeouts
policy.runners: matrix: /tmp/run_forksplit_matrix.sh (scripts/bench_matrix.py --mode run --wheel <wheel> --host-label ...); microbench: /tmp/run_qmm_pair.sh (direct /tmp/qmm_worker.py); both left in /tmp on jwm1-linux

limitations: 3 alternating pairs per leg vs the canonical 12-rep protocol; the 12-rep fork-vs-stock baseline is cited from receipts/2026-09-10-main-parity-12-matrix instead of re-measured, and my coop legs agree with its fork medians.

Kernel identity per arm rests on the MLX_OMARCHY_NO_COOPMAT gate (the only difference between arms), the 3.4-3.6x kernel-level timing separation, and the targeted-capability logs in receipts/2026-09-10-prefill-qmm-isa; MLX_OMARCHY_GPU_PROFILE NDJSON is only emitted by --diagnostics wheel builds, so no GPU-timestamp stream exists for the release wheel.
Three single-cycle decode outliers (max 2.169) are published unfiltered with their structural explanation rather than dropped.
one q4_short coop sample (250.0 of 333.3/250.0/333.3) is a low outlier retained in the medians and samples above.
